item.summary: The European Banking Authority (EBA) on 25 November 2026 published a report on the use of e-money tokens (EMTs) and other selected stablecoins in decentralised finance (DeFi). The EBA says stablecoins, including some EMTs issued under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), are used for liquidity, collateral and settlement in DeFi trading and lending, and that it has identified consumer-protection and regulatory-arbitrage risks, including around the prohibition on paying interest on EMTs. EU consumer participation in DeFi remains limited, the EBA says, but access is becoming easier through crypto-asset service providers, and the release states that 42% of European-based investors are expected to engage with DeFi by 2028. The EBA reiterates its recommendation that the European Commission, in its review of MiCA, assess whether additional requirements should apply to CASPs that facilitate access to DeFi, in particular lending protocols.
